correctness.rationale: The Fourier eigenvalues and on-shell scattering Möbius formula were checked against the full Exner–Turek–Tater source (2018, §§3,5). Circulant permutation rigidity and conjugate modal pairs force no global phase, and the sign of the upper-semicircle modes excludes every cyclic power except R. The modal match k=tan(v)/tan(tv) is strictly increasing in v for 0<t<1, giving the full degree classification. A Taylor expansion at t=k=1 and strict least-squares projection yield exact d_n and C_n>0; uniform k-endpoint gaps and strict local Hessian give a unique global momentum optimum near t=1. The embedded independent matrix solver and Fourier formula agree in 106 checks; finite tests are corroborative, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The prior 2018 paper supplies the underlying U(t) and S(k), but not the nontrivial exhaustive exact deterministic-routing classification across degrees and detunings, nor the globally optimized near-endpoint leakage coefficient. The 2017 endpoint and 2024 periodic-chain results address related but different questions. Source full text and targeted research-record comparisons were performed; possible uninspected equivalent analyses remain a residual priority risk.
residual_risks: The existing general on-shell formula strongly covers pointwise scattering and could support another author independently deriving the classification; publication-wide priority cannot be established from searched material.
Not every remotely related quantum-network publication or unpublished calculation was accessible; search absence is not proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The degree threshold answers a natural deterministic-circulator feasibility question with clear physical geometry and quantifier scope: matching two distinct Fourier phase pairs is impossible when n>=5. The strict positive globally optimized leakage constant is the natural quantitative obstruction, measuring best obtainable routing probability near an otherwise perfect endpoint, not an arbitrary computation. It yields explicit leading corrections for network design and is not a mere small numerical increment to a known table.
